headline: THE LLC: DAMAGE ON THE BALANCE SHEET
copy:
“Is Babb coming?”
“No confirmed booking. No confirmed journey.”
“So the only man we're talking about can't walk in and defend himself.”
“Then don't put words in his mouth.”
“I wasn't going to.”
(Beat.)
“...I was going to do an impression.”
“Don't.”
fact: A company with a history of winning. A franchise currently struggling. And one very empty interview chair.
visual: original host at desk; clearly empty guest chair; a production manager standing near a stack of documents. Location unapproved: no identifiable skyline or established roads.

headline: HOLD ON. HE USED TO WIN.
copy:
HOST: “Ten and three in 2018. Third place. Nine and four in 2019. Fourth. In 2021? Nine and five. Third again. You can't call that a lucky week. The man built real teams.”
MANAGER: “Then why are you calling him a fraud?”
HOST: “Because I hadn't read the good pages yet. Fantastic. That's our whole problem.”
visual: Archival ledger copies with season-specific franchise aliases; not a fictional championship trophy.

headline: SIX FEET TO THE LEFT
copy:
MANAGER: “There's more than a record. Their office took damage. The wall was repaired. Babb moved his desk six feet.”
HOST: “Six feet? That's a man who knows where the trouble came through.”
MANAGER: “That's what Chapter Two records. It doesn't tell us where the desk is today.”
HOST: “Right. A repair bill is history. Not a live camera feed.”
fact: Approved Novel Chapter II; World State Ledger Week 2 boardroom repairs and Week 3 Storm City protection history.
visual: Illustrated archival document/schematic of historic damaged boardroom. Do not depict present-day damage as current fact, or invent a real interview prop obtained from Babb.

headline: GREAT PROJECTIONS. ROUGH REALITY.
copy:
HOST: “Ten and four in 2024. Second seed. Finished seventh. Not fake wins—real wins with a lousy ending.”
MANAGER: “And 2025?”
HOST: “Projected first. Finished four and ten.”
MANAGER: “This year?”
HOST: “Projected second. Two and five through Week Seven. Eleventh. Apparently the only thing expanding is the list of people asking what happened.”
HOST: “Six wins in twenty-one games since the start of last season. One season isn't even finished. I'm not holding a funeral. I'm asking for a different accountant.”
fact: 2024: 10–4 (2nd seed; 7th final); 2025: 4–10 (10th final); 2026 through W7: 2–5 (11th current).
visual: Paper earnings statement beside fantasy ledger; no literal TV monitors or unapproved modern technology.

headline: EVERYBODY'S GOT SOMEWHERE TO GO
copy:
HOST: “Slob beat The LLC in the preliminary Week Seven report. Fine. But next week Babb draws Red Leopards. ObiWan gets El Niño. Chili gets Three Dreaded Snake. Slob faces His Majesty's Blood. Duckhook gets Mud Dogs. D0nkey K0ng meets Seven Deadly Chins.”
MANAGER: “That's all twelve.”
HOST: “That's the point. It's not twelve scores. It's twelve people who came from somewhere and have to live with what comes next.”
visual: Typographic broadcast schedule with a map only if supported active routes; no implied individual travels to match venues. No fabricated Week 8 outcomes.

headline: PAST PERFORMANCE. FUTURE QUESTIONS.
copy:
MANAGER: “So what's the story?”
HOST: “A guy who knew how to build a winner. A company that took a hit and kept its papers in order. And a football team that's having a hard time remembering the first part.”
MANAGER: “You want to ask him?”
HOST: “Yeah. But you can't manufacture the conversation. If Babb ever gets here, let him use the front gate.”
HOST: “And if he beats Red Leopards, we put that in next week's report, too. We don't get to stop time because we found a punchline.”
fact: “This has been After Dark. Past performance does not guarantee future results. Apparently neither do the projections.”
visual: Empty chair, closed copied ledger, quiet stage. No guest silhouette implying secret attendance.
